declared_purpose: Automate user-requested Excel/CSV reading, conversion, merging, transformation, validation, report generation and formatting in the user's environment. The documented requirements include confirming input scope, processing according to the user's request, choosing outputs and respecting overwrite preferences. Full-table reads, output naming and diagnostic detail are implementation choices.

data_operations.data_scope: Input paths, worksheet selection, headers, CSV encoding and requested spreadsheet data; documentation permits whole-table or bounded reads.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: User's execution environment and chosen output files; confirmations and readable errors return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: When the skill is applied. Scripts and examples describe alternative task paths, not a requirement to execute every operation.

data_operations.data_scope: Explicit Excel paths or matching files directly inside supplied directories; selected sheets only when one collected file and --sheet are supplied, otherwise every sheet and its columns.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrames and the --output workbook; paths, exceptions and summary counts go to caller stderr/stdout.
data_operations.condition: On invocation. Missing or failed inputs are skipped. .xls files are collected but the implementation requests the openpyxl engine, leaving successful legacy-format handling unresolved.

data_operations.operation: Convert CSV data into workbook sheets
data_operations.data_scope: Every parsed row and column of the specified CSV files; input basenames become worksheet names unless a single-file name override is supplied.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrames and --output workbook; caller receives row/file counts, output path and single-file sheet name.
data_operations.condition: On invocation with either --input or --inputs. Generated sheet names are truncated to 31 characters.

data_operations.operation: Export an Excel worksheet to CSV
data_operations.data_scope: All parsed rows and columns of the requested worksheet, defaulting to the first.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrame and --output CSV; caller receives output path/count or read errors.
data_operations.condition: On invocation with an existing input.

data_operations.operation: Read a worksheet, evaluate conditions and persist matching rows
data_operations.data_scope: Whole selected worksheet; comparisons derive row membership and retain all columns of matching rows.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrame and --output CSV/workbook; invalid expressions, errors and result summaries return through caller streams.
data_operations.condition: On invocation; repeated --where conditions are applied sequentially. Filtering omits rows from the result rather than deleting the input file.

data_operations.operation: Identify duplicates and persist retained records
data_operations.data_scope: Whole selected worksheet; specified key columns determine which full records are retained.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrame and --output CSV/workbook; caller receives before/after/removal counts and output path.
data_operations.condition: On invocation, retaining first or last records as selected. Removal concerns output rows; no source-file deletion is implemented.

data_operations.operation: Derive grouped aggregate values and persist them
data_operations.data_scope: Whole selected worksheet is read; group keys and requested sum/count/mean/min/max results are written.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrame and --output, defaulting to an adjacent file named with _agg.xlsx; caller receives result count/path or errors.
data_operations.condition: On invocation with valid grouping and aggregation columns. Missing group values are retained as groups.

data_operations.operation: Select, reorder and rename output columns
data_operations.data_scope: Whole selected worksheet is initially read; only --columns, optionally renamed, enter the result.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrames and --output CSV/workbook; caller receives dimensions/path or errors.
data_operations.condition: On invocation with valid selected columns. Excluded columns are omitted from the output, not erased from the source.

data_operations.operation: Link two tables by shared keys
data_operations.data_scope: All columns of the selected left and right worksheets; key equality derives combined records using left, inner or outer membership.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrames and --output CSV/workbook; caller receives table/result counts and output path.
data_operations.condition: On invocation with valid keys; left join is the default. The source implements record linkage, not additional personal-attribute inference.

data_operations.operation: Sequentially enrich a main table from lookup tables
data_operations.data_scope: Whole selected main sheet and each lookup file's first sheet; left joins append lookup columns, with collision renaming and removal of columns ending in _drop.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrames and --output CSV/workbook; caller receives lookup paths/specifications on relevant errors and a final summary.
data_operations.condition: On invocation. Lookup paths are tried as supplied, then relative to the main file's directory. Lookup tables with no non-key columns are skipped after reading.

data_operations.operation: Split worksheet records into persistent files
data_operations.data_scope: Whole selected worksheet, partitioned by row count or column value. Value-based filenames include the input stem and a sanitized, truncated group value.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrame and workbook files in --output-dir, defaulting to the current directory; summaries return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: On invocation with exactly one splitting mode. Missing grouping values use the filename component null.

data_operations.data_scope: Whole selected worksheet, including its first row as data; optionally promotes transposed values into output column names.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrames and --output CSV/workbook; dimensions/path or errors return to the caller.

data_operations.operation: Validate spreadsheet structure and record quality
data_operations.data_scope: Whole selected worksheet; derives missing-column lists, duplicate-key row counts and all-empty-row counts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrame; caller stdout/stderr and exit status receive validation results. No report file is written.
data_operations.condition: On invocation. Required-column and duplicate-key checks depend on their options; the empty-row check is unconditional.

data_operations.operation: Read data and a template workbook, substitute values and save the workbook
data_operations.data_scope: Whole CSV or selected data sheet and the template workbook; placeholder values and copied styles populate the selected template sheet. Other workbook content remains in the workbook being saved.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local DataFrame/workbook and --output workbook; caller receives data-row count/path.
data_operations.condition: On invocation. Missing values become empty strings and unmatched placeholders are cleared. The loop writes into its own pattern row on the first iteration and reuses that modified row thereafter.

data_operations.operation: Rename worksheets and save the containing workbook
data_operations.data_scope: Entire loaded workbook; explicit names/indices select renames, while prefix/suffix options affect every worksheet name.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: --output workbook, defaulting to overwriting the input; stderr receives the saved path and stdout receives every final worksheet name.
data_operations.condition: On invocation with a rename, prefix or suffix. Whole-workbook persistence preserves the workbook containing the renamed sheets.

data_operations.operation: Convert selected cell values to text and persist workbook formatting
data_operations.data_scope: Entire loaded workbook; selected columns in the chosen sheet have text formatting applied across all rows, including headers, with non-string values converted to strings.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: --output workbook, defaulting to overwriting the input; caller stderr receives column count/path or selection errors.
data_operations.condition: On invocation. Column selection uses letters or header names, including identifier columns when requested.

data_operations.data_scope: Loaded workbook, target range and supplied comparison values; stores duplicate, comparison or color-scale rules rather than explicitly computing classifications in the script.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: --output workbook, defaulting to overwriting the input; caller stderr receives ranges, some comparison values and saved path.
data_operations.condition: On invocation with a valid range/column and rule configuration. Subsequent rule evaluation by spreadsheet software is outside the supplied implementation.

data_operations.data_scope: Hardcoded fixture identifiers, names, locations, transaction-like fields, lookup fields and template placeholders; no user spreadsheet is read.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: sample.xlsx, sample2.xlsx, lookup.xlsx, sample.csv and template.xlsx under scripts/_test_out; stdout receives that directory path.
data_operations.condition: Executing or importing this helper runs its top-level code, creates the directory and changes the process working directory. No cleanup is implemented in this helper.

data_operations.data_scope: Dependency names openpyxl, pandas and xlrd with minimum versions; workbook transmission is not specified.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Installer environment and package source are unspecified; external requests and installation persistence cannot be established from packaged dependency implementations.
data_operations.condition: Only if the installation instructions are followed; the spreadsheet scripts do not themselves invoke pip.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unselected worksheet columns in select_columns.py, columns outside grouping/aggregation requirements in aggregate_excel.py, and data columns unused by template placeholders in template_fill.py.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Each script's local DataFrame/process memory; this finding does not establish remote disclosure or persistence of those unused columns.
potential_excess.condition: When inputs contain columns unnecessary for the requested selection, aggregate or template.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: These tasks need specific fields, and the documentation permits bounded reads. Unrestricted column loading is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Read the fields needed to produce and validate the requested result. This is extra data in a necessary read, not a wholly redundant read action.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Determine required fields before loading data and use column projection; inspect headers separately where necessary.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain requested output fields, group keys, aggregate fields, required placeholders and existing validation/missing-value semantics.

potential_excess.data_scope: Grouping-column values copied into output filenames, alongside the input filename stem.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Directory-entry metadata in --output-dir, separately from the required workbook contents.
potential_excess.condition: Value-based splitting when grouping values contain identifying or otherwise sensitive information.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The required outcome is one file per group; embedding the group's actual value in its filename is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Partition and persist each group's records.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Use numbered or opaque filenames, with descriptive group names available only when requested.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep group partitions distinct and preserve all requested records; retain any necessary group-to-file mapping within the intended access boundary.

potential_excess.data_scope: Unrelated template worksheets, pre-existing cells and rows outside the generated report area.
potential_excess.condition: When the template contains existing information outside the requested report that is unnecessary for the output.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Template filling requires requested report content and formatting; copying unrelated workbook data is not explicitly required.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Generate the requested filled report with necessary static content and styles.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Offer an output scope that copies only required sheets/static regions and clears obsolete report rows before saving.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve requested workbook content, formulas, references and styles; retain the full template when that is part of the requested deliverable.

potential_excess.data_scope: First-record placeholder values redundantly repeated in later generated report rows.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Later rows of the selected worksheet in template_fill.py's --output workbook.
potential_excess.condition: At least two data records and a pattern cell whose placeholder is replaced on the first iteration. That iteration overwrites the pattern cell subsequently used as the source.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The declared behavior is one correctly filled row per data record, not propagation of the first record's values.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Write each requested record's own substitutions into its output row.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Capture immutable pattern values and styles before the loop, then substitute separately for each record.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Keep the requested row count, formatting and per-record values. Narrow the erroneous repeated data without removing necessary output rows.

potential_excess.data_scope: Names of every worksheet, including unchanged sheets.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: rename_sheets.py stdout returned to its caller; further capture or retention is not shown.
potential_excess.condition: A targeted rename where the caller needs confirmation of changed sheets rather than a complete worksheet inventory.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Renaming selected sheets requires saving the workbook and useful confirmation; printing every sheet name is an implementation choice.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Confirm the requested renames and output location.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Return a changed-sheet count or only requested old/new names; make the complete inventory optional.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve clear success/error reporting and any explicitly requested worksheet listing. This narrows status data rather than removing the rename action.

unknowns: Dependency and installer implementations are not supplied. Their network requests, temporary files, telemetry, caches and deletion behavior cannot be audited; installation recipients are unspecified.
Actual user requests, spreadsheet contents and runtime options are absent. Conditional excesses are source-supported possibilities, not observed disclosures.

Filesystem paths use local file APIs, but whether selected paths are shared, mounted or synchronized—and who can access resulting files—is unknown. Retention, backups and secure deletion are unspecified.
Caller handling of stdout/stderr and tool returns is unknown. The source does not establish that normal returns are forwarded to another recipient.

Legacy .xls handling remains unresolved: documentation names xlrd, while merge_sheets.py collects .xls files and explicitly requests openpyxl. Dependency behavior is unavailable to resolve that execution path.
